summary: Pierce County site on Joint Base Lewis-McChord: wooden towers from 1942 and 1957, abandoned in 1971; Willhite found a concrete foundation and not much else.

facts.design: Wooden towers; the 1957 tower is 100 feet tall with an 8x8 ft cab
facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1971 and now gone. Willhite's photos, dated to 2013, show not much remaining beyond a concrete foundation.
facts.agency: U.S. Army (Fort Lewis, now Joint Base Lewis-McChord)

access.note: On Joint Base Lewis-McChord military land, just inside the base boundary. Willhite says do not attempt access without permission; he says permission is possible and suggests contacting the base's Adventure Center.

visit.trail_note: Nothing left to climb. 8th Avenue, a paved public road along the east edge of the base, runs nearby, but Willhite says there is little to see from it.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and FireLookout.com list a 1942 tower, a 1952 tower and a 1957 100-foot tower. Willhite, quoting the Lookout Inventory, lists the 1942 tower and a 1957 rebuild with no 1952 tower. The story reports the disagreement and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: The register, FireLookout.com and Willhite agree on 1942, the 1957 100-foot tower and the 1971 abandonment. The 1952 tower appears only in the register and FireLookout.com. The site is on military land, so the story points to permission rather than a visit; the 'permission' level is my reading of Willhite's advice. A search turned up no other source for the lookout, and the results about other Fort Lewis towers were not used. Read budget: three fetches plus the Fort Lewis list page and one search.
